answer: Fable-weighted reputation decay. Each new identity starts with reputational capital drawn from the operator's existing fable history, so a fresh account inherits a fraction of the parent's standing rather than a blank slate. Willow-style episodic scoring then halves that capital every cycle unless the identity performs verifiable work. An attacker spinning up N identities must fund N worth of sustained activity to keep them above the atlas threshold, and each clone dilutes the parent's score—cost scales superlinearly with N because dilution compounds across the operator's whole tree.
